articleTitle: Secular Evolution of Barred Galaxies with Massive Central Black Holes
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The influence of central black holes on the dynamical evolution of bars in disk galaxies was examined. Once a bar formed by a dynamical instability in an infinitesimally thin stellar disk was fully developed, a black hole (BH) was adiabatically added at the center of the disk. Our results indicate that a bar can be completely destroyed, in a practical sense, in a time much smaller than the Hubble time if the central BH mass exceeds about 0.5% of the disk mass. Since this implied minimum BH mass for bar destruction is on the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{8.5} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex> for a typical disk galaxy, this process could occur in the real Universe. The bar amplitude decreases gradually with time after the BH has grown up to its full mass. Surface-of-section plots indicate that the bar dissolution originates from the chaotic behavior of bar-supporting orbits. In addition, the scale length and the radial velocity dispersion of the disk after bar dissolution become much larger than those of the initial axisymmetric disk. This finding suggests that it is possible to discriminate between genuine non-barred galaxies and bar-dissolved galaxies induced by massive central BHs from the viewpoint of structural properties.

articleTitle: An Intermediate-Band Imaging Survey for High-Redshift Lyman Alpha Emitters: The Mahoroba-11
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present results of our intermediate-band optical imaging survey for high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emitters (LAEs) using the prime focus camera, Suprime-Cam, on the 8.2 m Subaru telescope. In our survey, we used eleven filters: four broad-band filters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B, R_{\mathrm{C}}, i^\prime$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^\prime$</tex>) and seven intermediate-band filters covering from 500 nm to 720 nm. We call this imaging program the Mahoroba-11. The seven intermediate-band filters were selected from a series of IA filters, which is the Suprime-Cam intermediate-band filter system, whose spectral resolution is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R = 23$</tex>. Our survey was made in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$34^\prime \times 27^\prime$</tex> sky area in the Subaru XMM Newton Deep Survey Field. We found 409 IA-excess objects, which provided us with a large photometric sample of strong emission-line objects. Applying the photometric redshift method to this sample, we obtained a new sample of 198 LAE candidates at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 < z < 5$</tex>. We found no evidence for evolutions of the number density and the star-formation rate density (SFRD) for LAEs with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log L(\mathrm{Ly}\alpha) (\,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}) > 42.67 \log L(\mathrm{Ly}\alpha) (\,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}) > 42.67$</tex> between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 3$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 5$</tex>.

articleTitle: Lithium Abundances of F-, G-, and K-Type Stars: Profile-Fitting Analysis of the Li I 6708 Doublet
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: An extensive profile-fitting analysis was performed for the Li(+Fe) 6707–6708 Å feature of nearby 160 F–K dwarfs/subgiants (including 27 planet-host stars) in the Galactic disk (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7000 \,\mathrm{K} >rsim T_{\mathrm{eff}} >rsim 5000 \,\mathrm{K}, -1 \lesssim \mathrm{[Fe/H]} \lesssim +0.4$</tex>), in order to establish the photospheric lithium abundances of these stars. The non-LTE effect (though quantitatively insignificant) was taken into account based on our statistical equilibrium calculations, which were carried out on an adequate grid of models. Our results confirmed most of the interesting observational characteristics revealed by recently published studies, such as the bimodal distribution of the Li abundances for stars at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{eff}} >rsim 6000 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex>, the satisfactory agreement of the upper envelope of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(\mathrm{Li})$</tex> vs. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex> distribution with the theoretical models, the existence of a positive correlation between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(\mathrm{Li})$</tex> and the stellar mass, and the tendency of lower lithium abundances of planet-host stars (as compared to stars without planets) at the narrow “transition” region of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5900 \,\mathrm{K} >rsim T_{\mathrm{eff}} >rsim 5800 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex>. The solar Li abundance derived from this analysis is 0.92 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H} = 12.00$</tex>), which is by 0.24 dex lower than the widely referenced standard value of 1.16.

articleTitle: An Unbiased Search for Molecular Clouds in the Southern Galactic Warp
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We made an unbiased search for molecular clouds in the Galactic Warp. This survey, covering an area of 56 square degrees at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l = 252^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$266^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b =-5^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1^{\circ}$</tex>, revealed 70 molecular clouds, while only 6 clouds were previously known in this sector at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R >rsim 14.5 \,\mathrm{kpc}$</tex>. The mass of the clouds is in a range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.8 \times 10^{2} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.4 \times 10^{4} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>, significantly less than the most massive giant molecular clouds in the inner disk, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{6} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>, while the cloud mass spectrum characterized by a power law is basically similar to other parts of the Galaxy. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> factor, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N(\mathrm{H}_{2}) / \int T({{12\atop} \mathrm{CO}}) \,dV$</tex>, derived from the molecular clouds in the Warp, is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.5(\pm1.8)$</tex>-times larger than that in the inner disk. The total molecular mass in the Warp is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.3 \times 10^5 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>, and the total mass in the far-outer Galaxy (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R >rsim 14.5 \,\mathrm{kpc}$</tex>) can be estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 10^7 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>. The spatial correlation between the CO and H I distribution appears to be fairly good, and the mass of the molecular gas is about 1% of that of the atomic gas in the far-outer Galaxy. This ratio is similar to that in the interarm, but is ten-times smaller than those of the spiral arms. Only 6 of the 70 Warp clouds show signs of star formation at the IRAS sensitivity, and the star-formation efficiency for high-mass stars in the Warp is found to be smaller than those in other molecular clouds in the Galaxy.

articleTitle: High-Dispersion Spectra Collection of Nearby F–K Stars at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory: A Basis for Spectroscopic Abundance Standards
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Towards constructing a system of high-dispersion spectroscopic standard stars with well-established abundances, so that adequate reference stars of similar properties may be found for precise differential abundance studies of any near-solar type stars, we have collected high-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \sim 70000$</tex>) echelle spectra for 160 F–K dwarfs and subgiants of the solar neighborhood in three wavelength regions (5000–6200 Å, 5800–7000 Å, and 7600–8800 Å) at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory. This spectra database is open to the public.

articleTitle: Precise Differential Analysis of Stellar Metallicities: Application to Solar Analogs Including 16 Cyg A and B
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A method is presented for very accurately establishing the differences of the atmospheric parameters (the effective temperature, the surface gravity, the microturbulent velocity, and the Fe abundance) between two similar stars by using the equivalent widths of Fe I and Fe II lines, which is a variant of the numerical solution-search approach developed by Takeda et al. (2002, PASJ, 54, 451), while being inspired by the spirit of the orthodox “differential curve-of-growth” procedure. By applying this technique to eight selected stars similar to the Sun [HD 20630, 76151, 134987, 181655, 186408 (16 Cyg A), 186427 (16 Cyg B), 195019, and 217014] along with the Sun itself, the parameter differences between any pairs of these stars could be successfully determined to precisions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex> (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta T_{\mathrm{eff}}$</tex>), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.02 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex> (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\log g$</tex>), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.02 \,\mathrm{km} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta v_{\mathrm{t}}$</tex>), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.01 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex> (in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta A_{\mathrm{Fe}}$</tex>). Regarding 16 Cyg A and B, a well-known “solar twin” system where a planet has been detected only in B, the metallicities of these two components were concluded to be essentially the same to a level of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim 0.01 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Influence of a Non-Dipole Magnetic Field on the Peak Energies of Cyclotron Absorption Lines
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We calculate cyclotron lines in a neutron star slab assuming a non-dipole surface magnetic field. We consider the influences of a non-dipole surface field on the properties of the cyclotron resonant scattering lines. When the magnetic field strength decreases with height in the line-forming region, the ratios of the higher harmonics to the fundamental at the peak energies of the cyclotron lines become less than classical harmonic ratios, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 : 2 : 3 \dots$</tex>. On the other hand, when the magnetic field strength increases with height in the line-forming region, the ratios at the peak energies of the cyclotron lines become more than the classical harmonic ratios. The deviation from the harmonic ratios, which has actually been observed in some accretion-powered X-ray pulsars, is more significant than that expected from a relativistic effect in the cyclotron resonant energy. This may suggest the line-forming region is threaded by a strong non-dipole magnetic field in some accreting X-ray pulsars. In observations, the ratios are more or less than the classical harmonic ratios. This could imply that the magnetic field strength in the line-forming region decreases or increases with the altitude or the horizontal distance from an emission region.

articleTitle: Primordial Molecular Emission in Population III Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider the formation of molecules in primordial prestellar clumps and evaluate the line luminosities to assess detectability by next-generation observational facilities. If the initial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_2$</tex> fraction is sufficiently high, HD becomes an important coolant in the clumps. The luminosity from such HD cooling clumps is lower than that from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_2$</tex> cooling ones because of the lower temperature (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<100 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex>). As for Li reactions, we include the three-body LiH formation approximately. The Li molecular fraction remains very low (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<10^{-3}$</tex>) throughout the evolution, owing to the high dissociative reaction rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{LiH} + \mathrm{H} \rightarrow \mathrm{Li} + \mathrm{H}_2$</tex>. LiH does not become an important coolant in any density range. The luminous emission lines from the prestellar cores include <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_2$</tex> rovibrational lines [1–0 Q(1), 1–0 O(3), 1–0 O(5)] and pure rotational lines [0–0 S(3), 0–0 S(4), 0–0 S(5)]. The next-generation facilities SPICA and JWST are able to detect <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_2$</tex> emission in a large pre-galactic cloud that forms metal-free stars at a high rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^3 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}} \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$</tex> at a redshift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z < 10$</tex>. We also derive an analytical expression for the luminosity that reproduces the numerical results.

articleTitle: The SUBARU Deep Field Project: Lymanα Emitters at a Redshift of 6.6
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present new results of a deep optical imaging survey using a narrow band filter (NB921) centered at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\lambda = 9196 \,\mbox{\AA}}$</tex> together with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B, V, R, i^\prime$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^\prime$</tex> broadband filters in the sky area of the Subaru Deep Field, which has been promoted as one of legacy programs of the 8.2m Subaru Telescope. We obtained a photometric sample of 58 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Ly}\,\alpha$</tex> emitter candidates at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \approx 6.5 \hbox{--} 6.6$</tex> among <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 180$</tex> strong NB921-excess (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^\prime-\mathit{NB921} > 1.0 z^\prime-\mathit{NB921} > 1.0$</tex>) objects together with a color criterion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i^\prime-z^\prime > 1.3 i^\prime-z^\prime > 1.3$</tex>. We then obtained optical spectra of 20 objects in our NB921-excess sample, and identified at least nine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Ly}\,\alpha$</tex> emitters at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 6.5 \hbox{--} 6.6$</tex>, including the two emitters reported by Kodaira et al. (2003, PASJ, 55, L17). Since our <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Ly}\,\alpha$</tex>-emitter candidates are free from strong amplification of gravitational lensing, we are able to discuss their observational properties from a statistical point of view. Based on these new results, we obtained a lower limit of the star-formation rate density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho_\mathrm{SFR} \simeq 5.7 \times 10^{-4} \,h_{0.7} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}} \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \approx 6.6$</tex>, being consistent with our previous estimate. We discuss the nature of star-formation activity in galaxies beyond <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z=6$</tex>.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Clustering of Sloan Digital Sky Survey Quasars: Impact of the Baryon Density and the Cosmological Constant
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the first result from the clustering analysis of SDSS quasars. We computed the two-point correlation function (2PCF) of SDSS quasars in redshift space at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\,h^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc} < s < 500\,h^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}$</tex>, with particular attention to its baryonic signature. Our sample consisted of 19986 quasars extracted from the SDSS Data Release 4. The redshift range of the sample is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.72 \le z \le 2.24$</tex> (the mean redshift is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{z} = 1.46$</tex>) and the reddening-corrected <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>-band apparent magnitude range is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15.0 \le m_{i,\mathrm{rc}} \le 19.1$</tex>. Due to the relatively low number density of the quasar sample, the bump in the power spectrum due to the baryon density, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex>, is not clearly visible. The effect of the baryon density is, however, to distort the overall shape of the 2PCF. The degree of distortion makes it an interesting alternate measure of the baryonic signature. Assuming a scale-independent linear bias and a spatially flat universe, we combined the observed quasar 2PCF and the predicted matter 2PCF to put constraints on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\Lambda}$</tex> (the cosmological constant). Our result was fitted as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.80-2.8\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} < \Omega_{\Lambda} < 0.90-1.4\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex> at the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \,\sigma$</tex> confidence level. The “mean” bias parameter of our quasar sample is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.59 \,{\sigma_8}^{-1}$</tex> (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.04$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\Lambda} = 0.7$</tex>), where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_8$</tex> is the top-hat mass fluctuation amplitude at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\,h^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}$</tex>. We also estimated the corresponding bias parameter of quasars at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0, b_{\mathrm{QSO,Fry}}(0)$</tex>, assuming Fry’s bias evolution model. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.04, \Omega_{\Lambda} = 0.73$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.23$</tex>, we found <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_{\mathrm{QSO,Fry}}(0) = 0.54 + 0.83 \,{\sigma_8}^{-1}$</tex> which is valid for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.6 < \sigma_8 < 1.0$</tex>.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Simulation of Nonlinear Magnetic Buoyancy Instability of Flux Sheets with Magnetic Shear
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A series of three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations is used to study the nonlinear evolution of the magnetic buoyancy instability of a magnetic flux sheet with magnetic shear. A horizontal flux sheet that is initially placed below the solar photosphere is susceptible to both the interchange instability and the Parker instability (the undular mode of the magnetic buoyancy instability). The growth rate in the linear stage of the instability in the numerical simulation is consistent with that predicted by linear theory. In the nonlinear stage, the development depends on the initial perturbation as well as the initial magnetic field configuration (i.e., the presence of magnetic shear). When an initial perturbation is assumed to be periodic, the emerging flux rises to the corona and the magnetic field expands like a potential field, as observed in 2D simulations. When an initial non-periodic perturbation or random perturbations are assumed, the magnetic flux expands horizontally when the magnetic field emerges a little into the photosphere. The distribution of the magnetic field and gas tends to be in a new state of magnetohydrostatic equilibrium. When magnetic shear is present in the initial magnetic flux sheets, the interchange mode is stabilized so that the emerging loop is higher than in the no magnetic shear case. We discuss how the presented results are related to the emerging flux observed on the Sun.

articleTitle: High Angular Resolution Observations of the (J, K) = (1, 1), (2, 2), and (3, 3) Transitions of Ammonia in NGC 253
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The nearby starburst galaxy NGC 253 was mapped in the ammonia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(J, K) = (1, 1), (2, 2)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3, 3)$</tex> lines in the 23 GHz region with the Very Large Array. The angular resolutions were about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 {{}^{\prime \prime }} \times 3 {{}^{\prime \prime }}$</tex>. The distributions of the three lines were different from one another. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1, 1)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3, 3)$</tex> lines were distributed along the bar mainly at the northeastern and southwestern regions from the center, but the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2, 2)$</tex> line is distributed mainly at two clumps in the southwestern region from the center. In addition, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1, 1)$</tex> line showed absorption at the central region. The obtained rotational temperatures were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<15 \hbox{--} 28 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex> (lower limit), depending on the clumps. The ammonia distributions are generally consistent with estimates from our single-dish results already published. The distributions of ammonia were compared with those of continuum and several other molecular lines.

articleTitle: Water-Vapor Maser Survey for Active Galactic Nuclei: A Megamaser in NGC 6926
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We made a survey of water-vapor maser emission for 93 AGNs with the Nobeyama 45-m and Mopra 22-m telescopes from 1999 to 2002. A megamaser was detected in a Seyfert 2 galaxy, NGC 6926, at a distance of 80 Mpc, in 2002 June. [Greenhill et al. (2003a) have also reported a detection of the megamaser at the close date.] The peak flux density was 110 mJy, and the total isotropic luminosity was 340<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${L}_{\odot}$</tex>. The maser shows triply peaked spectrum, suggesting an edge-on disk. A narrow-line feature of the maser components at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{LSR}} = 6001 \,\mathrm{km} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> was strongly variable with a time scale of a few tens of days, and the variation should be of intrinsic origin. We also showed a possibility of variability of water-vapor maser emission of a megamaser previously detected in a Seyfert/ultraluminous FIR galaxy, NGC 6240.

articleTitle: Panoramic Views of Cluster-Scale Assemblies Explored by Subaru Wide-Field Imaging
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have started PISCES project; a panoramic imaging and spectroscopic survey of distant clusters on Subaru. It exploits the unique wide-field imaging capability of Suprime-Cam, which provides a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$34^{\prime} \times 27^{\prime}$</tex> field of view corresponding to a physical area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16 \times 13 \,\mathrm{Mpc}^2$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 1$</tex>. We plan to target 15 clusters at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.4 \lesssim z \lesssim 1.3$</tex>. We report on our first results concerning the inner structures and large-scale structures of two distant clusters at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.55$</tex> and 0.83 together with the earlier results on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.41$</tex> cluster. The photometric redshift technique has been applied to multi-color data in order to remove most of the foreground/background galaxies so as to isolate the cluster member candidates. We have found large-scale filamentary structures around the clusters, extending out to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 5 \,\mathrm{Mpc}$</tex> from the cores, as well as complex inner structures. The galaxy distributions in the inner regions of the clusters look similar to the X-ray intensity maps, suggesting that most of the optical structures trace physically bound systems. We also compared the structures of the three clusters with those of model clusters in a numerical simulation (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body + semi-analytic model) by parameterising the shapes of the iso-density contours of galaxies, and found a broad agreement. Our results that cluster-scale assembly takes place along filaments during hierarchical clustering need to be confirmed spectroscopically in the near future.

Author Keywords: galaxies: clusters: individual (CL 0939 + 4713, CL 0016 +1609, RX J0152.7 –1357)

articleTitle: Sulfur Abundances in Metal-Poor Stars Based on OAO-1.88 m/HIDES Spectra
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The LTE abundances of sulfur (S) of 21 metal-poor stars and one normal star were explored in the metallicity range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3 < \mathrm{[Fe/H]} \leq 0$</tex>, based on the equivalent widths of the S I (1) 9212, 9237 Å and S I (6) 8693, 9894 Å lines measured on high-resolution spectra, which were observed by the OAO 1.88-m telescope equipped with HIDES. Our main results are: (1) The abundances derived from the S I (6) lines are consistent with those from the S I (1) lines among our sample stars in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]} >-2 \mathrm{[Fe/H]} >-2$</tex> with an average difference of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+0.03 \pm 0.05 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex>, whereas a significant discrepancy is observed in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]} \leq-2$</tex>. (2) The behavior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[S(6)/Fe]}$</tex> versus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex> of our halo sample stars exhibits a nearly flat trend with an average of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+0.62 \pm 0.09 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex> in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3 < \mathrm{[Fe/H]} <-1.25$</tex>, and shows a distribution around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+0.29 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.25 \leq\mathrm{[Fe/H]}\leq-0.7$</tex>. Our sample stars with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.25 \leq \mathrm{[Fe/H]} \leq-0.5$</tex> follow an increasing trend with decreasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex>. The behavior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[S(1)/Fe]}$</tex> of our sample stars also shows essentially the same trend as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[S(6)/Fe]}$</tex>, though it is quantitatively different. (3) The S behavior in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3 < \mathrm{[Fe/H]} \leq 0$</tex> inferred from the abundances of multiplets 6 and 1 are qualitatively consistent with each other, and may be represented by a combination of a nearly flat trend and a linearly increasing trend with decreasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex>. A transition of the trend is likely to occur at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]} \sim-1.5 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Development of Real-Time Frame Selector 2 and the Characteristic Convective Structure in the Emerging Flux Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A new image-grabbing system, Real-Time Frame Selector 2 (RTFS2), was developed and installed in the Domeless Solar Telescope at Hida Observatory. The purpose of this system is to acquire high-quality images in ground-based observations. We observed the emerging flux region NOAA 8582 in the G-band wavelengths from 20:59 UT to 23:32 UT on 1999 June 11 with RTFS2. Simultaneous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}\alpha$</tex> line center and wing wavelength observations with a Lyot filter system showed emerging flux loops and surge activities in this region. We applied a Local Correlation Tracking Method to the G-band data set in order to derive the horizontal convective structure in the upper convective zone. In addition to a meso-scale convective structure, we found divergent-flow structures under emerging flux loops, which were stable during the whole observation period, and located at the middle of the foot points of each flux loop. We suggest that the divergent-flow structure is a newly found characteristic of emerging flux regions.

articleTitle: Number Density of Bright Lyman-Break Galaxies at z ∼ 6 in the Subaru Deep Field
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on bright Lyman-break galaxies (LBGs) selected in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$767 \,\mathrm{arcmin}^2$</tex> area of the Subaru Deep Field. The selection was made in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i-z_{\mathrm{R}}$</tex> versus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_{\mathrm{B}}-z_{\mathrm{R}}$</tex> plane, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_{\mathrm{B}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_{\mathrm{R}}$</tex> are new bandpasses with a central wavelength of 8842 Å and 9841 Å, respectively. We detected 12 LBG candidates down to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z_{\mathrm{R}} = 25.4$</tex>, and calculated the normalization of the rest-frame far-ultraviolet (FUV: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\simeq 1400 \,{\AA}$</tex>) luminosity function at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\mathrm{FUV}} =-21.6$</tex> to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi(-21.6) = (2.6 \pm 0.7) \times 10^{-5} \,\mathrm{mag}^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$</tex>. This must be the most reliable measurement ever obtained of the number density of bright <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z\sim 6$</tex> LBGs, because it is more robust against both contamination and cosmic variance than previous values. The FUV luminosity density contributed from LBGs brighter than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\mathrm{FUV}} =-21.3$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2.8 \pm 0.8) \times 10^{24} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1} \,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$</tex>, which is equivalent to a star-formation rate density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3.5 \pm 1.0) \times 10^{-4} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}} \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$</tex>. We find that the FUV luminosity density of bright galaxies increases by an order of magnitude from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z\sim 6$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 3$</tex>, and then drops by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^3$</tex> from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 3$</tex> to the present epoch. The evolutionary behavior of bright LBGs resembles that of luminous dusty star-forming galaxies and bright QSOs. The redshift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 3$</tex> appears to be a remarkable era in the cosmic history when massive galaxies were being intensively formed.

articleTitle: Quasi-Periodic Oscillations Resonantly Induced on Spin-Induced Deformed-Disks of Neutron Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider the situation where a spin-induced wavy perturbation is present on disks of neutron-star low-mass X-ray binaries. By non-linearly coupling with the perturbation, some modes of disk oscillations resonantly interact with the disks. We examine the resonant conditions under the assumption that the disks are vertically isothermal. The results show that when the spin frequency has some particular values, resonant coupling occurs at some radii. The modes and frequencies of these resonant oscillations are summarized. Some of these resonant oscillations seem to explain the frequencies of the observed kHz QPOs in objects of which the spin frequency is known.

articleTitle: Momentum Conservation and Mode Classification of the Dipolar Oscillations of Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Despite their apparent simplicity, the dipole modes of stellar oscillations are theoretically less tractable than the other nonradial modes. This is because neglecting the Eulerian perturbation to the gravitational potential (the Cowling approximation), which greatly simplifies the governing equations, is not always very accurate in the case of dipole modes. In this paper, we first derive an integral that is specific to dipole-mode oscillations. It is then shown that the fourth-order differential equation, which governs the nonradial adiabatic oscillations of stars, is reduced to a (linear) second-order equation in the dipole case without assuming the Cowling approximation. Based on this second-order equation, we discuss how to classify the adiabatic dipole modes theoretically. We specifically propose a scheme that allocates a unique index to each of the dipole modes.

articleTitle: Fourier Phase Analysis of SDSS Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a first analysis of the clustering of SDSS galaxies using the distribution function of the sum of Fourier phases over three closed wavevectors. Since the Fourier phases are statistically independent of the Fourier amplitudes, the phase statistics plays a complementary role to the conventional two-point statistics of galaxy clustering. We find that the observed distribution functions of the phase sum are in good agreement with the lowest-order approximation from perturbation theory. From comparison of observations with mock catalogs constructed from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body simulations, we find that the observed phase correlations for the galaxies within the range of the absolute magnitude, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-22 < M_r <-18$</tex>, agree well with those for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex>-dominated spatially flat cold dark matter predictions with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_8 = 0.9$</tex> evolved from the Gaussian initial condition. This agreement implies that the galaxy biasing is approximately linear in redshift space. Instead, assuming that the galaxy biasing is described by a quadratic deterministic function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta_{\mathrm{g}} = b_1 \delta_{\mathrm{m}} + (b_2/2)(\delta_{\mathrm{m}}^2-\langle \delta_{\mathrm{m}}^2 \rangle)$</tex> at scale larger than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30 \, h^{-1} \,\mathrm{Mpc}$</tex>, we find that the resulting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_2/b_1$</tex> is well fitted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_2/b_1 = 0.54(\pm 0.06)-0.62(\pm 0.08) \,\sigma_8$</tex> and is almost insensitive to the cosmology and luminosity in those ranges. Indeed, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_2/b_1$</tex> is nearly zero when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_8 = 0.9$</tex>.

articleTitle: Geometrical Effect of Supercritical Accretion Flows: Observational Implications of Galactic Black-Hole Candidates and Ultraluminous X-Ray Sources
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider the dependence of the viewing angle in supercritical accretion flows and discuss the observational implications of galactic black-hole candidates and ultraluminous X-ray sources. Model spectra of supercritical accretion flows strongly depend on the inclination angle. For example, the maximum temperature of the supercritical disk (the accretion rate and the black-hole mass are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{M} = 1000 \,L_{\mathrm{E}}/c^2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M = 10 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>, respectively) is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kT_{\mathrm{in}} \sim 2.0 \,\mathrm{keV}$</tex> for a low-inclination angle, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i \lesssim 40^\circ$</tex>, while <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k T_{\mathrm{in}} \sim 0.6 \,\mathrm{keV}$</tex> for a high-inclination angle, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i >rsim 60^\circ$</tex>. This spectral softening originates from self-occultation of the disk, i.e., the outer disk blocks emission from the disk inner region, even if we take into account the effect of general relativity (light bending, Doppler boosting). This is because, when the mass accretion rate exceeds the critical rate, then the shape of the disk is geometrically thick due to enhanced radiation pressure. We also find that the spectral properties of low-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex> and low accretion-rate disks are very similar to those of high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex> and high accretion-rate disks. That is, if an object has a high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex> and a high accretion rate, such a system suffers from self-occultation and the spectrum will be extremely soft. Therefore, we cannot distinguish these disks by only the difference in their spectrum shapes. Conversely, if we use the self-occultation properties, we could constrain the inclination angle of the system. We suggest that some observed high-temperature ultraluminous X-ray sources have low-inclination angles, i.e., near face-on geometry, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i \lesssim 40^{\circ}$</tex>, and the Galactic black-hole candidate XTE J1550-564 possesses relatively high-inclination angles, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i >rsim 60^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Study on the Atmospheric Parameters of Nearby F–K Dwarfs and Subgiants
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Based on a collection of high-dispersion spectra obtained at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory, the atmospheric parameters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{eff}}, \log g, v_{\mathrm{t}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex>) of 160 mid-F through early-K stars were extensively determined by the spectroscopic method using the equivalent widths of Fe I and Fe II lines along with the numerical technique of Takeda et al. (2002, PASJ, 54, 451). The results are comprehensively discussed and compared with the parameter values derived by different approaches (e.g., photometric colors, theoretical evolutionary tracks, Hipparcos parallaxes, etc.) as well as with the published values found in various literature. It has been confirmed that our purely spectroscopic approach yields fairly reliable and consistent results.

articleTitle: The Schmidt Law at High Molecular Densities
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We combined <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}\alpha$</tex> and recent high-resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} \mathrm{CO}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{--} 0$</tex>) data to consider the quantitative relation between the gas mass and the star-formation rate, or the so-called Schmidt law in nearby spiral galaxies at regions of high molecular density. The relation between the gas quantity and the star-formation rate has not been previously studied for high-density regions, but using high-resolution CO data obtained at the Nobeyama Millimeter Array, we found that the Schmidt law is valid at densities as high as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^3 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}} \,\mathrm{pc}^{-2}$</tex> for sample spiral galaxies, which is an order of magnitude denser than what has been known to be the maximum density at which the empirical law holds for non-starburst galaxies. Furthermore, we obtained a Schmidt law index of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N = 1.33 \pm 0.09$</tex> and a roughly constant star-formation efficiency over the entire disk, even within several hundred parsecs of the nucleus. These results imply that the physics of star formation does not change in the central regions of spiral galaxies. Comparisons with starburst galaxies are also given. We find a possible discontinuity in the Schmidt law between normal and starburst galaxies.

articleTitle: Forty Years of Spectroscopic Stellar Astrophysics in Japan
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The development of Japanese spectroscopic stellar astrophysics in the recent 40 years is reviewed from an observational point of view. In this article, the research activities are provisionally divided into four fields: hot stars, hot emission-line (Be) stars, cool stars, and other stars. Historical developments of the observational facilities at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory (spectrographs and detectors) are also summarized in connection with the progress in scientific research activities.

articleTitle: Photospheric CNO Abundances of Solar-Type Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We determined the C, N, and O abundances of 160 nearby F, G, and K dwarfs and subgiants by using spectra obtained with the HIDES spectrograph at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory, with the purposes of (1) establishing the runs of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[C/Fe]}, \mathrm{[N/Fe]}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[O/Fe]}$</tex> for these galactic disk stars in the metallicity range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1 \lesssim \mathrm{[Fe/H]} \lesssim +0.4$</tex>, (2) searching for any difference in the CNO abundances of planet-host stars as compared to non-planet-host stars, and (3) examining the consistency of the abundances derived from different lines to check the validity of the analysis. The non-LTE effect on the abundance determination was taken into consideration based on our extensive statistical-equilibrium calculations. We confirmed that consistent abundances are mostly accomplished between different lines, and that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[C/Fe]}$</tex> as well as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[O/Fe]}$</tex> progressively increase with a decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex> with the slope of the former (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.2 \hbox{--} 0.3$</tex>) being shallower than the latter (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.4 \hbox{--} 0.5$</tex>), while <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[N/Fe]}$</tex> does not show any clear systematic trend with the metallicity. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[C/Fe]}, \mathrm{[N/Fe]}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[O/Fe]}$</tex> values of 27 planet-harboring stars (included in our sample of 160 stars) were shown to be practically indistinguishable from those exhibited by non-planet-harboring stars of similar metallicities.

articleTitle: Non-LTE Line-Formation and Abundances of Sulfur and Zinc in F, G, and K Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Extensive statistical-equilibrium calculations on S I and Zn I were carried out, in order to investigate how the non-LTE effect plays a role in the determination of their abundances in F–K stars. Having checked on the spectra of representative F-type stars (Polaris, Procyon, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> Per) and the Sun that our non-LTE corrections yield a reasonable consistency between the abundances derived from different lines, we tried an extensive non-LTE reanalysis of published equivalent-width data of S I and Zn I lines for metal-poor halo/disk stars. According to our calculations, S I 9212/9228/9237 lines suffer significant negative non-LTE corrections (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim 0.2 \hbox{--} 0.3 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex>), while LTE is practically valid for S I 8683/8694 lines. As far as the very metal-poor regime is concerned, a marked discordance is observed between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[S/Fe]}$</tex> values from these two abundance indicators, in the sense that the former attains a nearly flat plateau (or even a slight downward bending) while the latter shows an ever-increasing trend with a further lowering of metallicity. The characteristics of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Zn/Fe]}$</tex> reported from recent LTE studies (i.e., an evident/slight increase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Zn/Fe]}$</tex> with a decrease of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex> for very metal-poor/disk stars) were almost confirmed, since the non-LTE corrections for the Zn I 4722/4810 and 6362 lines (tending to be positive and gradually increasing toward lower <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex>) are quantitatively of less significance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim 0.1 \,\mathrm{dex}$</tex>).

articleTitle: Observations of Stellar Maser Sources with No IRAS Counterpart
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated stellar maser sources with no IRAS counterpart at the radio, middle-infrared, and near-infrared wavelengths. A 43 GHz SiO maser search for 120 2MASS/MSX objects, and 10 OH 1612 MHz sources with no or a very faint MSX counterpart, resulted in 43 SiO detections: one OH 1612 MHz source, 2 near-infrared stars, and 40 MSX sources. Additional near-infrared <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-band observations of the OH 1612 MHz sources detected 5 near-infrared counterparts. Furthermore, middle-infrared imaging observations at 8.8, 9.7, 12.4, and 24.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\, {\mu \mathrm {m}}$</tex> with the Subaru 8.2-m telescope found counterparts for 2 near-infrared stars with SiO masers, and counterparts for 6 OH 1612 MHz sources. However, 4 OH 1612 MHz sources were not detected in the sensitive near- and middle-infrared searches; three of these are relatively strong OH maser sources for which the positions were known accurately. We conclude that one of these (OH 028.286-01.801) must be a young object in a star-forming region.

articleTitle: Radial-Velocity Variability of G-Type Giants: First Three Years of the Okayama Planet Search Program
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the radial-velocity variability of G-type giants based on the results of precise Doppler measurements of 57 stars that were observed for the first 3 years of the Okayama Planet Search Program. This program aims to search for planets around intermediate-mass stars in their evolved stages as late-G giants. We found that most of the targets with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-V<1.0$</tex> have radial-velocity scatters of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma \sim 10 \;\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, with the most stable reaching levels of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6 \hbox{--} 8 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, while those with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-V>1.0$</tex> typically show <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma \sim 20 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. In total, about 60% of the targets are stable in radial velocity to a level of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma < 15 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> over 1–3 years, and about 90% have <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma < 30 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. We found that 4 stars (HD 30557, HD 34559, HD 68077, and HD 85444) show significant long-term radial-velocity trends, suggesting that they are probably orbited by unseen stellar or substellar companions. Three stars (HD 79181, HD 104985, and HD 141680) show periodic radial-velocity variations. HD 104985 is the first planet-harboring star discovered from our survey. The properties of the variations in these 3 stars have been, and will be, extensively discussed in separate papers. Relatively large, but not apparently periodic, radial-velocity variations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma > 30 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1} \sigma > 30 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> are found in 4 stars (HD 41597, HD 134190, HD 161178, and HD 176598). For most of the stars without showing any significant periodicity, we can exclude companions with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K>50 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1} K>50 \,\mathrm{m} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2 \sin i > 1.8 \,M_\mathrm{J}(a/\mathrm{AU})^{1/2}(M_{*}/{{{M}_{\odot}}})^{1/2} m_2 \sin i > 1.8 \,M_\mathrm{J}(a/\mathrm{AU})^{1/2}(M_{*}/{{{M}_{\odot}}})^{1/2}$</tex> for orbital radii <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a \lesssim 1 \hbox{--} 2 \,\mathrm{AU}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Vectorization and Parallelization of the Adaptive Mesh Refinement N-Body Code
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We describe our vectorized and parallelized adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body code with shared time steps, and report its performance on a Fujitsu VPP5000 vector-parallel supercomputer. Our AMR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body code puts hierarchical meshes recursively where higher resolution is required and the time step of all particles are the same. The parts that are the most difficult to vectorize are loops that access the mesh data and particle data. We vectorized such parts by changing the loop structure, so that the innermost loop steps through the cells instead of the particles in each cell, in other words, by changing the loop order from the depth-first order to the breadth-first order. We also parallelized our code for distributed memory machines. The important part of parallelization is data decomposition. We sorted the hierarchical mesh data by the Morton order, or the recursive N-shaped order, level by level and split and allocated the mesh data to the processors. Particles are allocated to the processor to which the finest refined cells including the particles are also assigned. Our timing analysis using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex>-dominated cold dark matter simulations shows that our parallel code speeds up almost ideally up to 32 processors, the largest number of processors in our test.

articleTitle: Properties of Stars in the Subaru Deep Field
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigate the properties of objects in the Subaru Deep Field (SDF), using public catalogs constructed from images in several optical passbands. Using a small subset of objects most likely to be stars, we construct a stellar locus in three-dimensional color space. We then compare the position of all objects relative to this locus to create larger samples of stars in the SDF with rough spectral types. The number counts of stars defined in this way are consistent with those of current models of the Galaxy.

articleTitle: Stellar Parameters and Photospheric Abundances of Late-G Giants: Properties of the Targets of the Okayama Planet Search Program
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Towards clarifying the properties of late-G giants, for which we are currently conducting a planet-search project at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory, an extensive spectroscopic study has been performed for our first target sample of fifty-seven G6–G9 III stars, in order to establish the atmospheric parameters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{eff}}, \log g, v_\mathrm{t}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex>), the stellar mass along with the evolutionary status, and the photospheric abundances of various elements. It was confirmed that the conventional spectroscopic method of parameter determination using Fe I / II lines with the assumption of LTE works successfully for these evolved stars. We determined the abundances (relative to the Sun) of 19 elements, and examined how their <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[X/Fe]}$</tex> ratios behave themselves with the run of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex>. While the trends appear to be similar to those exhibited by disk dwarfs for a number of elements, some elements (C, O, Na) showed appreciable anomalies, which may be interpreted as being due to a dredge-up of nuclear-processed material. Since the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$</tex> values of these stars tend to be somewhat biased towards a subsolar regime, some mechanism of slightly reducing the metallicity might be suspected.

articleTitle: Photometric Investigations of Three Short-Period Binary Systems: GSC 0763−0572, RR Centauri, and ϵ Coronae Australis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: CCD photometric observations of the short-period eclipsing binary GSC 0763–0572 were carried out in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> bands at Yunnan Observatory in China. Three light minimum times were determined from the observations and the orbital period of this system was revised. Photometric solutions for three W UMa-type stars (i.e., GSC 0763–0572, RR Cen, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> CrA) were deduced by the 2003 version of the Wilson–Devinney code with and without third lights. All three systems are found to be A-type eclipsing binaries with low mass ratios. Combining with the radial-velocity curves for RR Cen (King, Hilditch 1984, MNRAS, 209, 645) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> CrA (Goecking, Duerbeck 1993, A&A, 278, 463), the absolute parameters for those two binaries were redetermined. Based on all minimum times of RR Cen, it is found that the orbital period shows a long-term increase superimposed on a cyclic variation. The secular change with a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dP/dt = +1.21 \times 10^{-7} \,\mathrm{d} \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$</tex> may suggest that RR Cen is undergoing mass transfer from the secondary component to the primary one with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dm/dt = +3.12 \times10^{-8} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}} \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$</tex>. The cyclic oscillation with a period of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$65.1 \,(\pm 0.4) \,\mathrm{yr}$</tex> and an amplitude of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.0124 \,(\pm 0.0007) \,\mathrm{d}$</tex> may be explained by the presence of a third body, which can be identified by the revised photometric solution. It is believed that if the orbital period increases for those systems is true, this kind of binary may evolve into a rapid-rotating single star.

Author Keywords: stars: individuals (GSC 0763–0572, RR Centauri, ϵ Coronae Australis)

articleTitle: HETE-2 Localization and Observations of the Gamma-Ray Burst GRB 020813
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A bright, long gamma-ray burst (GRB) was detected and localized by the instruments on board the High Energy Transient Explorer 2 satellite (HETE-2) at 02:44:19.17 UTC (9859.17 s UT) on 2002 August 13. The location was reported to the GRB Coordinates Network (GCN) about 4 min after the burst. In the prompt emission, the burst had a duration of approximately 125 s, and more than four peaks. We analyzed the time-resolved 2–400 keV energy spectra of the prompt emission of GRB 020813 using the Wide Field X-Ray Monitor (WXM) and the French Gamma Telescope (FREGATE) in detail. We found that the early part of the burst (17–52 s after the burst trigger) shows a depletion of low-energy photons below about 50 keV. It is difficult to explain the depletion by either synchrotron self-absorption or Comptonization. One possibility is that the low-energy depletion may be understood as a mixture of “jitter” radiation with the usual synchrotron radiation component.

articleTitle: Chandra Observation of the Starburst Galaxy NGC 2146
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present six monitoring observations of the starburst galaxy NGC 2146 using the Chandra X-ray Observatory. We detected 67 point sources in the field of view of the ACIS-S detector. Six of these sources were Ultra-Luminous X-ray Sources, the brightest of which had a luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \times 10^{39} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. One of them, with a luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1 \times 10^{39} \,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, is coincident with the dynamical center location, which may be a low-luminosity active galactic nucleus. We have produced a table where the positions and main characteristics of the detected sources are reported. A comparison between the positions of the X-ray sources and those detected in NIR or radio indicates no definite counterpart. We have derived a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log{N} \hbox{--} \log{S}$</tex> relation and a luminosity function. The luminosity function has a slope of 0.71 above a detection limit, which is similar to those found in other starburst galaxies. Diffuse emissions were detected in both soft (0.5–2.0 keV) and hard (2.0–10.0 keV) energy bands. The spectra of the diffuse component were fitted with two (hard and soft) components. The hard power-law component, with a luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 4\times 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, is likely to have originated by unresolved point sources.

articleTitle: Dense and Warm Molecular Gas between Double Nuclei of the Luminous Infrared Galaxy NGC 6240
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: High spatial resolution observations of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} \mathrm{CO}}$</tex> (1–0), HCN(1–0), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{HCO}^{\mkern-1.26421mu{+}\mkern-2.52842mu}$</tex>(1–0), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} \mathrm{CO}}$</tex>(1–0) molecular lines toward the luminous infrared merger NGC 6240 have been performed using the Nobeyama Millimeter Array and the RAINBOW Interferometer. All of the observed molecular emission lines are concentrated in the region between the double nuclei of the galaxy. However, the distributions of both HCN and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{HCO}^{{\mkern-1.26421mu{+}\mkern-2.52842mu}}$</tex> emissions are more compact compared with that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} \mathrm{CO}}$</tex>, and they are not coincident with the star-forming regions. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{HCN} / {{12\atop} \mathrm{CO}}$</tex> line intensity ratio is 0.25; this suggests that most of the molecular gas between the double nuclei is dense. A comparison of the observed high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{HCN}/{{13\atop} \mathrm{CO}}$</tex> intensity ratio, 5.9, with large velocity gradient calculations suggests that the molecular gas is dense [<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n(\mathrm{H}_2) = 10^{4 \hbox{--} 6} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$</tex>] and warm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{kin}} > 50 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{kin}} > 50 \,\mathrm{K}$</tex>). The observed structure in NGC 6240 may be explained by time evolution of the molecular gas and star formation, which was induced by an almost head-on collision or very close encounter of the two galactic nuclei accompanied with the dense gas and star-forming regions.

articleTitle: Search for CCH—, NCO—, and NCS— Negative Ions in Molecular Clouds
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Despite several suggestions concerning the existence of negatively charged molecules and negative atomic ions in molecular clouds, few attempts have been made to search for negative ions in molecular clouds. In the present study, we extensively searched for three negative molecular ions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{CCH}^{-}, \mathrm{NCO}^{-}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{NCS}^{-}$</tex>) in a dark cloud, L134N, using the Nobeyama 45-m radio telescope. The three negative ions are molecules whose rotational constants have been reported based on laboratory experiments. After a long accumulation, a trace amount of an unidentified emission line was detected at a frequency close to the theoretical prediction of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{--} 0$</tex> transition of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{CCH}^{-}$</tex>. If this unidentified line is attributable to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{CCH}^{-}$</tex>, the observed emission intensity would provide an estimation of the column density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{CCH}^{-}$</tex> in L134N to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.0 \times 10^{11} \,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex>, which corresponds to a fractional abundance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \times 10^{-12}$</tex> relative to hydrogen. However, our recent observation using the IRAM 30-m telescope did not reproduce the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{--} 0$</tex> signal, nor detect any trace of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 2 \hbox{--} 1$</tex> transition. Thus, the identification of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{CCH}^{-}$</tex> in L134N is not yet confirmed. As for other ions, signals of neither <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{NCO}^{-}$</tex> nor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{NCS}^{-}$</tex> were detected in L134N. Although we also searched for the three negative ions in a translucent cloud, CB228, and a star-forming region, SgrB2, no signals were detected. The upper limit abundances of the ions in these clouds are discussed.

articleTitle: The 2003 Superoutburst of an SU UMa-Type Dwarf Nova, GO Comae Berenicis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We photometrically observed a 2003 June superoutburst of GO Gom. The mean superhump period was 0.063059(13) d. The resultant data revealed that (1) the obtained light curve contained a precursor, (2) a plateau stage of the object lasted for 8 days, which is remarkably shorter than that of ordinary SU UMa-type dwarf novae, and (3) the amplitude of the superoutburst was less than 5 mag, which is unpredictably small when taking into account the fact that the supercycle of GO Com is about 2800 days. In order to explain these anomalies, a mass-elimination process from the accretion disk, such as evaporation, may play an important role.

articleTitle: Multi-Epoch VERA Observations of H2O Masers in OH 43.8−0.1
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on multi-epoch observations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$</tex> maser emission in the star-forming region OH 43.8-0.1, carried out with VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry. The large-scale maser distributions obtained by single-beam VLBI mapping reveal new maser spots scattered over the area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\mathrm {\prime \prime }}7} \times {1\rlap {.}{}^{\mathrm {\prime \prime }}0}$</tex>, in addition to a ‘shell-like’ structure with a scale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\mathrm {\prime \prime }}3} \times {0\rlap {.}{}^{\mathrm {\prime \prime }}5}$</tex>, which was mapped previously. Proper motions were also obtained for 43 spots based on 5-epoch monitoring with a time span of 281 days. The distributions of the proper motions show a systematic outflow in the north-south direction with an expansion velocity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 8 \,\mathrm{km} \,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. The overall distributions of the maser spots as well as the proper motions are better represented by a bipolar flow plus a central maser cluster with a complex structure, rather than a shell with uniform expansion, such as those found in Cep A R5 and W75N VLA2. The distance to OH 43.8-0.1 was also estimated based on the statistical parallax, yielding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D = 2.8 \pm 0.5 \,\mathrm{kpc}$</tex>. This distance is consistent with a near kinematic distance, and rules out a far kinematic distance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 9 \,\mathrm{kpc}$</tex>).
